---
slug: everything_was_okay
title: Everything Was Okay
blurb: An ordinary inspection day at a KYL unit factory turns grim when the lights cut out and the blast doors close, with Wade hiding behind a conveyor belt.
authors: Silas
season: FF4
format: prose
---

The assembly line was running normally, the next generation of KYL Units being manufactured. Gary, the factory manager, was in for his weekly inspection. Tracks were running smoothly. Workers were efficient enough, for how few there were. Only two accidents since the last inspection.

Wade worked diligently, double-checking the finished units for software malfunctions. He rarely ever found anything wrong; on occasion, one would have a logic issue and he’d send it back to maintenance.

“[Find anything today, Wade?]{Gary}” asked Gary, standing over Wade’s shoulder with a joyous expression.

“[No, boss, haven’t had a brain problem since Tuesday]{Wade},” Wade responded, looking behind him for a second before returning to work.

“[Excellent. Keep at it, son]{Gary},” Gary remarked. He walked away, likely to check on the innovation department, Wade presumed. People were always trying to think of new ways to build the same robot, maybe with a few improvements. [*It’s bullshit*]{Wade}*,* thought Wade, [*but that’s just how it is these days.*]{Wade} He knew that this job was what was keeping his life together, and he wasn’t going to risk it to complain that his company was following the standard formula for a business.

Wade kept at it for the next hour or two, working his standard shift, checking one mechanical brain after another. To his surprise, he heard Gary’s voice over the intercom:

“[*Hello, everyone, I’d just like to inform you that we’re getting a surprise check-up from Company Director Vince. He should arrive shortly. If we get a good rating from him, you’re all getting bonuses, so keep your head in the game. That’s all.*]{Gary}”

The building cheered, although there weren’t many workers. It was the best news Wade had heard in months. Maybe he could buy his wife an anniversary gift early? Or perhaps keep saving up for that new starship they had been looking at? His mind raced with possibilities, but he quickly returned to work, making sure to look as good as possible when the boss came in.

Another half-hour passed before the main doors opened to reveal a large figure covered in fur, its purple mane flowing down the classy suit it donned. Vince was here.

Wade noticed the boss’s arrival and made sure to look like he was working as hard as possible. Gary ran over to greet him, and began touring him, making sure he saw everything good and nothing bad in the factory.

Sweat began dripping down Wade’s forehead, his blonde hair shimmering as the stress built. He knew he was doing his job well, but there was always an unnerving feeling when Vince was here, especially due to his stature.

Seconds became minutes, minutes became hours. While the boss was in the building, everybody was on edge.

A few minutes later, Gary took Vince into the conference room, likely to receive a review of his management.

Without warning, the lights cut. The emergency power turned on, and the alarm system rang out:

[*Emergency - Power Outage - Emergency Battery Activated*]{Factory Alarm}

Wade sighed in relief—just an outage. Relatively typical, with how much power the station uses to run an assembly line like this.

[*Emergency - Security Breach Detected - Blast Doors Engaged*]{Factory Alarm}

In the dim red light of the emergency lights, Wade watched as the room was blocked off by large titanium doors. His heart began racing. He dropped to his knees and hid behind the conveyor belt, peering over his cover. He had never wanted to hear its obnoxious clanking whirr more than now. His mind began to race again: What’s happening? Is anybody hurt? Will I ever see my family again?

Something hit the blast door. So hard it left a dent in the thick plating. And again. And again.

Finally, the door burst open with a crash, the metal bending outwards with a metal fist thrust through the hole. With a grunt, the fist pulled open the hole larger, fitting the other fist through, and opened the hole wide enough to enter through.

A figure in black armor stepped through the door, stepping on the sheet of metal and crushing it to the floor so he could walk through. He was followed by three other, smaller figures in similar armor.

Wade began to hyperventilate and ducked back under the belt, horrified.

The figures made their way through the room, their heavy armor clanking with each step.

The terror was overpowering. Wade couldn’t stay quiet any longer—a whine escaped from him. Realizing what he had just done, he clasped his hands over his mouth.

“[There]{Ravens Leader},” spoke a deep, metallic voice. Wade heard footsteps coming his way. He knew this was his end. He curled up into a fetal position.

The footsteps drew closer. Before he knew it, they stopped and a shadow loomed over him. A figure in crimson armor bent down and grabbed him by the throat, lifting him into the air.

“[**Where is Vincent?**]{Odran}” the figure asked, feigning innocence as they closed Wade’s windpipe.

Frantically kicking and attempting to gasp for air, Wade pointed to the conference room. Only his own life mattered to him now.

“[**Thank you. Your death will be much less painful now**]{Odran},” the figure told him. Tightening their grip, the red-clad figure crushed Wade’s neck like a toothpick. His lifeless body slumped to the floor as the figure let go.

The four walked slowly toward the conference room. The one in black walked up to the door and slammed his fist into it, creating the same dent as before. He kicked it in the center and felt the structure weaken. Kicking it once more, the blast door flew backwards and slammed into the oval wooden table. The four walked into the room and stared into the eyes of the two cowering bosses.

“[Who the hell are you? Why are you here?!]{Gary}” screamed Gary.

The figures stared for a few seconds longer before the one in black spoke: “[**Marv, take care of him.**]{Ravens Leader}” The green character, apparently known as Marv, calmly walked up to the poor Elvish manager. Paralyzed with fear, Gary watched as Marv approached him. The menacing figure grabbed Gary by his right arm and clenched. Gary screamed in pain as an audible snap was produced from his arm, now obviously shattered. Marv continued by doing the same to his other three limbs before grabbing him by his screaming mouth, tugging the jaws in opposite directions before the lower jaw broke off, blood leaking from the severed meat.

The black-clad figure looked toward Vince.

“[P-please don’t hurt me, I’ll give you anything, tell you anything]{Vince},” he pleaded.

“[**You will answer this question or you will suffer: Where is Victor?**]{Ravens Leader}”

“[Victor? Victor who?]{Vince}”

“[**Strike One.**]{Ravens Leader}” The figure kneeled before Vince and unsheathed a dagger, stabbing him in his gut. Vince writhed in agony, the blade cutting deep into his flesh and slowly moving across.

“[**You know who I am referring to, Vincent. Tell me where he is**]{Ravens Leader},” responded the figure.

“[Really, I don’t know, please-]{Vince}” Vince spoke, the pain making it excruciating to talk.

“[**Strike Two.**]{Ravens Leader}” The figure slashed open the rest of Vince’s torso, blood gushing from his wound. He screamed, barely able to move. “[**Your wife and children on Eutreka will die if you don’t tell me. Victor Chomsky. Tell me where he is.**]{Ravens Leader}”

“[You crazy fuck… I haven’t talked to that guy in GUYs, not since the group broke up… Last I heard, he got with this group called the Vortox Pummelers with a KYL-300 Model…]{Vince}”

“[**Excellent. We’re through here.**]{Ravens Leader}” the menacing figure responded. “[**You ex-mafia bosses are so weak... Sascha, finish him off for me.**]{Ravens Leader}”

The figure in blue walked up to the dying man. Vince noticed an emblem on all of their shoulders: A black bird, surrounded by a red circle.

“[W-wait, you’re-!]{Vince}”

She put her fist around his skull, muffling his words, waited for a few seconds, and crushed it, as if it were made of paper. Blood gushed through the fingers of her gloves and flecks of bone dropped to the ground, surrounding the now beheaded boss. The four walked out, the red lights still flashing in the station.

“[**Sir, I think I heard of that group before. Didn’t they kidnap that lizard racer?**]{Odran}”

“[**Yeah, I think they did. And they’re led by a Squoatling. Llamanians made a big fuss about it.**]{Marv}”

“[**It doesn’t matter. We need to locate them and dispose of that pyromaniac.**]{Sascha}”

“[**Hush, all of you. They’re a bounty-hunting group, so all we need to do is put a contract out there. Let’s go...this light is hurting my eyes.**]{Ravens Leader}”

As the four exited the building, Wade’s body lay on the floor, his corpse playing a small part in the scene of the ravaged building. Nobody would come here for a while. He would rot, just like the rest, and he would be forgotten in time. What a shame.

***

Everything was okay.

Until the Ravens arrived.
